deep_dive.title: DCSA deep dive: the dual-track clearance, with questions to think about
deep_dive.description: A longer walk through the Learn DCSA deck. Between slides, question cards ask "why does it work this way?", and the next slide answers them. Narration is AI-generated. This is study material, not official DCSA guidance.
deep_dive.fallback_note: The MP4 fallback is the earlier silent, captioned 2:26 cut.

items.name: 01-dual-track-lock
items.title: Why your company and your people get cleared together | DCSA dual-track
items.description: A company can't get its facility clearance until its key managers get theirs, and those managers wait on the company. Here's how that lock works. Narration is AI-generated (NotebookLM). Study material, not official DCSA guidance.

items.name: 02-no-self-sponsor
items.title: You can't sponsor yourself for a facility clearance
items.description: A facility clearance starts with a sponsor: a government customer or a cleared prime with a real classified need. This short explains why you can't apply on your own. Narration is AI-generated (NotebookLM). Study material, not official DCSA guidance.

items.name: 03-day-20-clock
items.title: The Day 20 clock: why facility clearances stall early
items.short_title: The Day 20 clock and the KMP due date
items.description: Once you're sponsored, the clock starts on your package and your key managers' paperwork. Miss it, and the request can stall before it really begins. Narration is AI-generated (NotebookLM). Study material, not official DCSA guidance.

items.name: 04-package-quality
items.title: The paperwork choke point in a DCSA facility clearance
items.description: Incomplete ownership records, a DD 441 that doesn't match, or a sloppy SF 328 are the usual reasons a package bounces. Get these right the first time. Narration is AI-generated (NotebookLM). Study material, not official DCSA guidance.

items.name: 05-sf328-fifteen
items.title: The 15% line on the SF 328 (foreign ownership)
items.description: Foreign ownership questions on the SF 328 changed in 2025. This short covers what the 15% threshold means and why it matters for FOCI. Narration is AI-generated (NotebookLM). Study material, not official DCSA guidance.

items.name: 06-sead4-whole-person
items.title: The "whole person" rule in clearance decisions (SEAD 4)
items.description: Personnel clearances weigh 13 guidelines across a person's whole life, not one bad moment. This short explains how SEAD 4 frames that judgment. Narration is AI-generated (NotebookLM). Study material, not official DCSA guidance.
